verbs.description: Begin signing in to a provider Signs in with the person's account at `service`, and answers where they finish it (`SignInStarted`): `ChatGPT` by `OpenAI`'s one-time code, GitHub Copilot and Hugging Face by a code entered on their pages, Google Vertex AI and the Gemini API on Google's own page, and `OpenRouter` on its page, which hands back an API key. The server waits for the account to grant it, keeps the grant (or the key) in the workspace's vault and renews it there; no window ever holds a token. Only the person themselves may sign in.
verbs.label: Begin signing in to a provider

verbs.description: Run the workspace on this computer's model Links the model this computer's Agent models pane chose as the workspace's: the providers it asks without a key (a model it runs itself, a server on its network) join the workspace's, and the workspace's work runs on that choice. Only a computer of the person's answers it, from its own pane; answers the providers as a `ModelProviders`.
verbs.label: Run the workspace on this computer's model

verbs.description: Ask the workspace's model One turn, as the model the person chose for a request (else their default) answers it, with the key their vault keeps. The argument is an `agent_provider_config` model request; the answer is a `Result` of its response and its error as serde writes one (`{"Ok": ...}` or `{"Err": ...}`), so a refusal keeps the kind a window decides by (no provider yet, no key) and the words the person reads.
verbs.label: Ask the workspace's model

verbs.description: List the models this computer runs Asks the computer's model manager what it has installed, what it offers for this machine, and how far each setup has got. A computer without a manager answers `LocalModels::available` false and why.
verbs.label: List the models this computer runs
